expected_level_description: You can: - advocate for agile working - adapt how you design and conduct research to respond to the complexity of the product environment - understand the strategic decisions the team needs to make so you can design appropriate research - influence decisions about priorities and agile processes in the team

You can: - understand and help teams to apply a range of methods to analyse research data and synthesise findings - effectively engage sceptical colleagues in analysis and synthesis - advise on the choice and application of techniques, and can critique colleagues’ findings to assure best practice

You can: - help teams understand the diversity of users of government services - effectively include all kinds of users in appropriate research activities - advocate inclusive practices and help teams design and deliver accessible services that work for all users

You can: - evaluate the quality of research against accepted professional standards for user research - explain what good user research practice involves - give constructive feedback to other user researchers to ensure work meets good practice standards

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders

You can: - use a wide range of user research methods, and can help teams to adopt them - plan user research for services with challenging user needs and complex user journeys - advise colleagues on the choice and application of research methods to assure best practice

You can: - evaluate and choose approaches for building your team’s understanding of the user - advocate for user research with sceptical colleagues and stakeholders - help inexperienced teams to adopt user-centred practices - identify the most important challenges and opportunities for your team's service development - align research plans to address team priorities

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

skill: Ethical research with patients and care staff
expected_level_description: You can: - judge when research needs formal ethics or research governance approval and prepare what it needs - plan safe research with people in vulnerable circumstances, such as children, people with dementia, and people in crisis - plan research in clinical settings without disrupting care, working with clinical leads and care staff - support researchers to look after their own wellbeing after distressing sessions
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - carry out equality impact assessments - build inclusive teams and practices
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
